label: rem:benzene-assembly-spine
title: The $\gamma\gamma$-from-light assembly spine to benzene
html:
Remark. The \gamma\gamma-from-light assembly spine to benzene

Light initiates the assembly. The Breit–Wheeler process \gamma\gamma \to e^+e^- seeds a lepton pair. That energy feeds quark–antiquark production, whose confinement closes into the Borromean nucleon and, by meson exchange, the proton. Twelve nucleons bind into a ^{12}\mathrm{C} atom (the A \ge 3 binding closure), and carbon's four octet channels assemble molecules.

The molecular layer is parameter-free. Each covalent bond order is the cardinality of the saturated orthogonal-channel set — the bond order = LP active set identity. The fractional \pi of an aromatic ring is the lateral-\pi overlap of the embeddable knot operator, delocalised by the assembly projector.

Validated predictions

Running the spine end-to-end (witness benzene-assembly-spine) reproduces the observed structural bond orders with no fitted constant:

species construction predicted observed
acetylene \mathrm{C_2H_2} \sigma \perp \pi_x \perp \pi_y orthogonal triple 3 3
benzene \mathrm{C_6H_6} \lambda=(2,2,2)\vdash 6, D_6 ring \tfrac{3}{2} \tfrac{3}{2}
cyclohexane \mathrm{C_6H_{12}} saturated control 1 1

Acetylene's \mathrm{C}\!\equiv\!\mathrm{C} fills all three orthogonal channels (one axial \sigma, two transverse \pi). The spatial-dimension bound caps it at three. Benzene's six \mathrm{C\!-\!C} bonds come out identical. The D_6 symmetry of the assembly projector forces zero spread, so bond equalisation is a consequence of the construction, not an assumption. Aromaticity then registers as a +\tfrac{1}{2} bond-order increment per bond over the saturated ring. It consists of one localised \sigma plus a half-share of the delocalised six-electron \pi system.
